Serving as a Instructional Systems Specialist GS-1750-13 makes you a valuable member of the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) team and mission.

This position is located in the Office of the Associate Director for Training Ops (TOPS), Training Management Operations Directorate (TMO), eLearning and Training Analytics Division (ETA), eLearning and Evaluation Branch (EEB), located in Glynco, Georgia.

The primary purpose of this position is to serve as an Instructional Systems Specialist (ISS) responsible to oversee senior-level designer/developer/consultant and leader directly supporting research, design, development, evaluation, and implementation of training related initiatives within the eLearning and Training Analytics Division (ETA), Training Management Operations Directorate (TMO).

Typical duties include: Conducting training needs analyses, curriculum evaluations, and gap assessments for law enforcement professionals to ensure training programs align with mission objectives and address identified learning requirements.

Designing, developing, and implementing innovative training programs across multiple delivery formats (eLearning, instructor-led, hybrid, and virtual-live), applying adult learning theories and instructional systems design principles to create high-quality instructional materials.

Evaluating the effectiveness of training programs using established models (such as the Kirkpatrick model), collect and analyze data, and provide actionable recommendations to improve instructional quality and learner outcomes.

Managing and coordinating project teams in the development, delivery, and quality assurance of training initiatives, ensuring timely completion of deliverables and adherence to established standards.

Developing and delivering law enforcement training for international audiences, including engaging in international travel and collaborating with foreign law enforcement agencies to strengthen global training partnerships. (2) Leading the design and development of innovative training programs using adult learning theories, resulting in high-quality instructional materials that meet diverse learner needs across multiple delivery formats (i.e, eLearning, in-person, hybrid).

(3) Evaluating training effectiveness using established models such as Kirkpatrick, resulting in actionable data-driven recommendations that enhance instructional quality. (4) Managing project teams in the implementation of training initiatives, resulting in timely completion of deliverables and consistent adherence to quality assurance standards.

The Instructional Systems Specialist serves as the Training Development Program Manager and is responsible for establishing procedures and standards for training development projects and programs, managing training development projects, providing strategic advisory services to the Training Solutions Team Manager regarding development and maintenance of training programs, and leading training development and revision projects/programs of major significance in support of the FAA and external federal agencies.

The Instructional Systems Specialist is a recognized subject matter expert in developing and executing training development plans based on extensive knowledge of FAA training program standards and practices.

Acts as a principal specialist to develop new and innovative approaches, methodologies, and/or techniques of instructional design methods and processes, adult education theories and principles, and educational technologies, methods, and media.

Provides project management oversight to course development and other projects, including establishing requirements, budget, and schedule, identifying risks and recommending mitigations, monitoring scope, budget and schedule, communicating project status to management and stakeholders and recommending corrective actions as needed.

Reviews deliverables for quality and acceptability before closing out and documenting projects. Assigns tasks and prioritizes the work of multi-disciplinary training development teams for complex programs and projects that have inter-agency and often national impact.

The Training Development Program Manager applies experience and expert knowledge to conduct functional activities for programs that often require the development of new and innovative approaches. Identifies and resolves challenging problems or issues that often cross organizational boundaries and impact on the accomplishment of strategic objectives.

Oversees development of processes, plans, and templates to ensure uniformity and consistency of training products and adherence to national policies, standards, systems, and procedures governing FAA and external federal agencies' training.

Researches, analyzes, and recommends new training methods, media, and technology for integration into training programs. Identifies, acquires, and assigns resources for large projects/programs/work activities. Generates cost estimates for new projects.

Conducts studies and prepares reports on program management efficiency and effectiveness and makes recommendations regarding training program improvements that impact a wide range of training activities to ensure consistent, high-quality training.

Maintains an overall schedule of Training Solutions Team programs and reports progress, issues, and risks to the Training Solutions Team manager. Broad policies and objectives provide general guidance for addressing issues but often require the development of new approaches.

Provides program management oversight to include identifying risks and recommending mitigations. Provides expert guidance and instruction both internally and externally to address diverse, complex issues.

May develop new policies, procedures, and approaches that take into consideration FAA policies, Government-wide rules and regulations, and external concerns. Contacts are internal and external. Often represents the FAA Academy in meetings and is a principal point of contact for communications with internal and external stakeholders.

Speaks authoritatively on Academy training development policies, processes, and practices. Applies expertise in FAA training standards and practices, instructional design methods and processes, adult education theories and principles, and educational technologies, methods, and media.

Communicates the organization's vision and objectives and sets team priorities. Performs other duties as assigned.
Basic Requirements: Successful completion of a full 4-year course of study in an accredited college or university leading to a bachelor's or higher degree that was supplemented by at least 24 semester hours appropriate to the work of the position to be filled.

The coursework must have included study in AT LEAST FOUR OF THE FOLLOWING FIVE AREAS (Applicants MUST submit course descriptions from the appropriate college/university): 1) Learning theory, psychology of learning, educational psychology: Study of learning theories as they relate to the systematic design, development, and validation of instructional material. 2) Instructional design practices: Study of the principles and techniques used in designing training programs, developing design strategy and models, and applying design methods to the improvement of instructional effectiveness. 3) Educational evaluation: Study of the techniques for evaluating the effectiveness of instructional/educational programs, including developing written and performance tests and survey instruments, and determining reliability and validity of evaluation instruments. 4) Instructional product development: Study of the techniques appropriate for developing training materials, including identifying learner characteristics, specifying objectives, applying training strategy, validating training materials, and evaluating training. 5) Computers in education and training: Study of the application of computers in education and training, including selecting appropriate computer software.

Specialized Experience includes: Experience researching, evaluating and implementing new and innovative training technologies, methods, and media. Experience conducting studies and preparing reports on program management efficiency and effectiveness. Experience in coordinating and administering formal educational or training services programs.

Location: Remote Position Type: 12-Month Contract with the possibility of conversion to a permanent role Reports to: Director of Programs and Community Development About the Role Digital Moment is seeking a senior Learning Experience Designer to help us bring our learning content into a new era - designing applied AI education and translating powerful in-person learning experiences into effective self-paced digital learning on our platform.

Your anchor project is funded and concrete: design and produce a 40-hour applied AI apprenticeship course.

This starts with building a modular, competency-based AI curriculum system - a framework and module library covering AI foundations, practical AI use, responsible AI, and career pathways - with its first application serving a diverse cohort of youth who are not currently in education, employment, or training (NEET).

But the role is bigger than one course. Over the contract, you will help convert our existing catalog of educator and youth content into instructionally sound, self-paced digital experiences, and originate new content for audiences we're just beginning to serve — including parents, small businesses, and seniors.

You'll work embedded within our Programs team, partnering closely with Digital Product, and demonstrating what great digital learning looks like by building it. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who operates with autonomy, originates content rather than only adapting it, and wins people over by proof rather than persuasion.

What You'll Do 1. Design and deliver the AI apprenticeship course (anchor project)
Develop an applied AI competency framework: the knowledge, skills, behaviors, and confidence the curriculum builds, from foundational through intermediate levels.
Design a modular curriculum architecture - module categories, sequencing logic, standards for structure and assessment, and guidelines for combining modules into programs of different lengths and focuses.
Develop the library of learning modules across areas such as AI foundations, practical AI use (prompting, AI-supported workflows, no-code tools), responsible AI (ethics, bias, privacy, human oversight), and application pathways (problem-solving, sector use cases, careers, entrepreneurship).
Produce complete, delivery-ready learning materials, including a comprehensive facilitator guide that enables trained Digital Moment facilitators to deliver the program without you in the room, so it can scale across a growing facilitator network and be translated into self-paced digital formats.
Configure the modules into the apprenticeship pathway for our first cohort, including applied projects and a flexible capstone model, and validate coherence, pacing, and progression.
Build flexible assessment and impact-measurement tools (baseline/endline surveys, knowledge checks, rubrics) aligned with program and funder reporting needs.
2. Adapt the catalog for digital
Convert existing educator and youth content into instructionally sound, self-paced learning experiences on our digital platform.
Design within platform constraints and in step with the platform roadmap, in close partnership with our Digital Product Manager.
Establish reusable patterns and standards for in-person-to-digital conversion that others can follow.
3. Originate content for new audiences, ensuring inclusivity and cultural awareness
Build toward learning experiences for new audiences over time, including parents sole proprietors, and seniors.
Originate new content where no in-house playbook exists, working with program staff as subject-matter reviewers and validating with real users (e.g., advisory groups, user testing).
Design for self-directed adult learners: low-time, motivation-driven, and coming in with widely varying confidence and AI literacy.
4. Measure, maintain, and model
Gather participant and facilitator feedback; iterate on modules and materials.
Keep AI-related content current as tools, workplace practices, and learner needs evolve.
Work embedded in the Programs group, building confidence in digital learning through visible, high-quality delivery.
Who You Are We are looking for a rare mix of technical know-how and human-centric education experience. If you meet most of these qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Instructional Design & Digital Learning
Strong instructional-design / learning-science foundation, with demonstrated experience converting in-person training into digital and e-learning formats.
Experience designing modular, competency-based curricula or learning systems — not only individual courses.
A portfolio of learning artifacts you have created (course modules, facilitator guides, e-learning experiences, assessment tools, or equivalent).
Applied AI Expertise
Credible working proficiency with current AI tools and concepts — LLMs, generative AI tools, no-code/low-code applications, prompting, data literacy, and responsible AI — deep enough to author an applied AI course.
The ability to translate complex technical concepts into simple, engaging, everyday language, grounded in how AI is genuinely used across industries today.
Content Creation & Audience Range
Content creation and writing strength — you originate new material, not just adapt existing content.
Experience designing for adult and informal learners (self-directed, time-constrained, motivation-driven), not only K–12 settings.
Experience designing for or working with diverse and underserved learners — experience with marginalized, vulnerable, or NEET youth is a strong asset for the anchor project.
Bilingualism (English/French) is an asset.
How You Work
Senior individual contributor: self-directed, resourceful, comfortable owning outcomes with autonomy.
